title: Raw rational descent of a compatible integral refinement
statement: Fix a prime l, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l, a finite-field datum D with l different from its characteristic, finite-type D.k-schemes X,Y, and a separated finite-type D.k-morphism f:X to Y. Let R and F be the ring and rational coefficient construction records [def-sf-constructible-exceptional-coefficient-construction-data]. Fix compactifications c,d, and a shift-compatible natural isomorphism alpha_E between their integral left operations for every finite field stage E. Assume the integral alpha family commutes with the prescribed completed scalar q maps. Assume the localization comparison source and target shift structures agree for c,d and its q components have the literal identity normalization. Then there is a shift-compatible family beta_E of natural isomorphisms between the fixed rational left operations. On every integral representative beta is the raw localization of alpha, as HEq of components. For every finite field extension beta commutes with the prescribed rational scalar q maps. No ring refinement is constructed and no closed-stage comparison is asserted.

source.place: Section 5, Lemma 5.13 and Constructions 5.14--5.15; normalized refinement construction step 6.

proof.text: The coefficient prime is a unit on each residue field. Apply integral_residue_tor to identify the intrinsic integral and uniform finite-Tor predicates. Define the inverse of their inclusion by retaining the object and arrow and changing only the membership proof. Consequently rationalization from the finite-Tor category is surjective on objects.

On the intrinsic integral category conjugate the localized alpha by the inverse source q and the target q, precomposing with the explicit inverse inclusion. Apply naturalIso_of_integral to descend this natural isomorphism to the fixed rational operations. Its component formula and the two identity normalizations, with rationalAction supplying the endpoint equalities, give the required HEq with the localized integral alpha.

Use hX and hY to put both q comparisons under the same localization shift structures. Their shift compatibility and that of alpha imply shift compatibility of the conjugate. The component formula identifies this conjugate with the precomposition of beta. Cancel this precomposition using the object-surjectivity established in the first step (Mathlib NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft).

The integralScalar_eq field identifies each supplied integral scalar functor after ambient inclusion with the intrinsic completed scalar extension. Faithfulness and injectivity on objects of the full inclusion identify the intrinsic restricted functors. The object formula and the pure-tensor map formula at coefficient one for the fixed rational scalar extension then identify scalar extension after rationalization with rationalization after integral scalar extension. Apply rationalization to hs. The beta component formulas and rational_normalized identify its four factors with those of the rational square, with endpoint equalities from rationalAction and the scalar functor identity. Every rational object has an integral representative, so the square holds on every object.
